text:
Ava (CEO): Thanks for coming to the town hall. Opening this thread for quick follow-ups about mission, market positioning, competitors, and anything leadership promised to clarify. Keep it short — we'll answer through the day.

Zoe (Head of Product): Quick one: is our public messaging going to call out 'reserved capacity' as a product name or keep it as 'Dedicated / Reserved'?

Ava (CEO): Use 'Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)' in external docs to avoid confusion. Short-form: 'Dedicated'.

Marcus (Sales): For enterprise decks: are we allowed to say "predictable cost at scale" or do we need qualifiers?

Rafael (CTO): You can say it but include the qualifier: "based on workload patterns (batching, cache)". We want buyers to know it's about economics, not list price.

Jules (Eng): Roadmap nit: when will model rollback + canary routing be in Console for Private customers? they asked for it in the pilot.

Rafael (CTO): Canary routing + automatic rollback is planned for the next release cycle. Hosted first, then Dedicated/Private; ETA: ~6 weeks for Hosted beta, ~10-12 for Private GA.

Priya (Growth): Marketing needs a 1-line elevator: something crisp that contrasts us vs cloud-managed model endpoints. Any proposals?

Ava (CEO): Draft: "Redwood: predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Use as a base, tweak for brevity.

Marcus (Sales): International question: will the hosted product support regional data residency controls in APAC by end of year?

Rafael (CTO): Yes 1 region controls are on the roadmap. We plan to add configurable region routing and residency flags in Q4. Private remains the option for immediate residency guarantees.

Zoe (Head of Product): Competitor posture: should we publish head-to-head latency charts or prefer anonymized benchmarks and customer stories?

Ava (CEO): Prefer anonymized, reproducible benchmarks and concrete customer case studies. Head-to-head claims invite fast responses and legal scrutiny.

Jules (Eng): Metrics people keep asking for: what reliability numbers are public? uptime, mean-time-to-recover, fallback invocation rate?

Ava (CEO): Public: uptime and latency SLO attainment. Internal/partner docs: MTTx and fallback rates. Marketing will craft how to show those publicly with context.

Priya (Growth): Request: can leadership provide a 2-paragraph press blurb + 2-line sales pitch we can paste into outreach?

Ava (CEO): Yes. I'll drop a press blurb + sales lines by EOD. Tagging @Zoe to coordinate the exact wording.

Marcus (Sales): Pricing: any shift towards committed discounts vs pure usage? customers want predictable unit costs month-to-month.

Rafael (CTO): We're keeping both. Committed Dedicated contracts and usage tiers for Hosted. Optimize will recommend quantization/batching to reduce unit cost. Finance will publish standard discount bands.

Zoe (Head of Product): Data controls question for Private: will we support KMS + HSM integrations out of the box?

Rafael (CTO): Yes, KMS integrations supported. HSM planned as an add-on for regulated customers; timeline in the compliance roadmap doc.

Jules (Eng): Eval/quality workflow: are evals going to be part of the Console (so product teams can run regression checks)?

Zoe (Head of Product): Yes, Console will include prompt-set/eval hooks and regression alerts (first in Hosted, then Dedicated). ETA: alpha in 3 months.

metrics-bot: Note: parity checklist draft uploaded to /docs/internal/positioning/parity-checklist-v1.md

Priya (Growth): One last ask: can engineering provide a short matrix showing expected % cost reduction from batching at small/medium/large seq lengths? Sales needs numbers for calls.

Rafael (CTO): We'll provide a typical ranges table (e.g., 1.2x-2.5x cost reduction small seqs, 1.5x-3x medium, etc.) with a caveat about variance. Zoe/Meera will include it in the assets.

Ava (CEO): Thanks all. We'll consolidate assets (press blurb, sales lines, parity matrix) and post them here. If you have follow-ups, keep them tight and tag the relevant owner. :sparkles:
